text.p: A sharp further decline in grain rates for Panamaxes in the USGulf became apparent on Tuesday and as a result, after only an 8-day spell above the 1500 level, the Baltic Freight Index fell back 16 points to 1488.
Some brokers believed Atlantic rates have still further to fall, but others anticipated a spurt in enquiry shortly for first half December loading.

Meanwhile demand for Panamaxes remained firm in the middle and far East with some brokers reporting a resurgence in chartering enquiry from South Africa and Australia. Conditions for Capers were described as 'steady enough worldwide'.

The Handy market remained dull although some improvement may be anticipated in the South Atlantic with about 400,000 tonnes of wheat believed to be scheduled for export from Argentina before the end of the year.

GRAIN - Hanjin fixed a Seafreight vessel for 54,000 heavy grain USGulf/Japan for Dec 6/18 at $23.00 bas no combiantion, down from $24.10 reported overnight fixed with Bright Field by Goldbeam for Dec 1/10 and $25.25 with Istria by Dreyfus for end Nov at the end of last week.

USGulf/Continent rates were also said to have fallen heavily - Dreyfus were quoted as saying they had fixed a Panamax on subjects at $13.50 basis 55'. Other grain brokers reported Panamaxes available at between $13.50 and $14.00. Continental were reported having fixed a 1981-built Panamax delivery USGulf end Nov trip Continent only $9,000 daily plus $140,000 bonus.

But the continent offered better returns for owners - NNC took the 1980-built Ledra 61,981 dwt delivery prompt Ireland trip via North France and Egypt redelivery Passero at $11,000 daily and Irisl fixed the 1981-built Sun P 65,738 dwt delivery North France trip via U.K. and Iran redelivery passing Muscat at a firm $13,750 daily.

There were rumours that Iranian charterers had also covered a Panamax heavy grain cargo from Western Canada at $20.00. Solid rates for heavy grain were again reported in this area - Dreyfus fixed 52-54,000 Nopac/Japan at $16.00 no combination and MSK booked Hanjin tonnage for 54,000 Nopac/Taiwan at $16.80, both for early Dec loading.
Progress were said to have fixed a Panamax for prompt delivery South Brazil for 2-4 months on private terms. Handy-size activity in grain and other trades was negligible.

MINERALS - A number of Caper fixtures were completed but details were not made available - Docenave were linked with a vessel delivery Hampton Roads for 2 laden legs Atlantic trading, Jean L.D. with 150,000 ironore Port Cartier/Dunkirk West for end dec with Coe and Clerici, and Olivia 144,394 dwt spot Las Palmas was also fixed, but further information was lacking.
Intraf were rumoured to have booked Marshal Zhukov 103,307 dwt delivery Tubarao end Nov redelivery Eregli at only $6,250 daily plus $70,000 bonus.

Navalis 133,000 dwt open China mid Dec was rumoured fixed by Keoyang for short period timecharter. The Middle east was firm for Panamaxes - Navix agreed $12,000 daily on subjects for Petra 64,848 dwt delivery Aden Dec 1/10 for a trip via Goa with ironore to Japan and NSAC fixed Navarino 63,880 dwt delivery Bin Qasim Dec 15/30 for about 3-5 months in the region of $10,000/$10,250 daily.
Geeta 70,295 dwt was believed fixed for coal from Mobile to Ensted at $13.25, possibly with a second discharge port.
